title: Surface Roughness Analysis - Corrosion Detection on Puma 9900
subtitle: Post-Implant Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Michael Torres

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9900 system to detect and classify Corrosion defects during post-implant inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Corrosion defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9900 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9900
- Inspection Type: Surface Roughness Analysis
- Target Defect: Corrosion
- Process Step: Post-Implant
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all Puma 9900 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for post-implant monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9900
Software Version: v15.8.861
Recipe: SURFACE_ROUGHNESS_ANALYSIS_14nm_POST_IMPLANT
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (176 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9900 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Surface Roughness Analysis' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Corrosion defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 114 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 97% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.0% for Surface Roughness Analysis
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-08-22
Wafers Tested: 22
Total Defects Found: 176
Defect Density: 24.9 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.6%
Capture Rate: 86.3%
Test Duration: 394 minutes
System Uptime: 99.2%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9900 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Corrosion at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
